h: Know Before You Putt, and Where to Go Next
p: A couple of things to keep in mind before you go. If you're coming as a gang, think about splitting into smaller teams so nobody's stood about too long between shots, and you get a bit of friendly rivalry between teams as well as within them. Turn up a few minutes early to get your drinks in and avoid starting your round in a rush.

Think about whether you want golf to be the main event or the warm-up. A round makes a brilliant start to a night out, getting everyone chatting and laughing before you head off for food and drinks. It also works well as the finale, after a day of sightseeing has worn everyone out.

Liverpool has a huge choice for before and after. Bold Street is lined with independent cafés and restaurants serving dishes from across the globe, while the Baltic Triangle has a lively mix of creative spaces, bars and street food. For something truly Liverpool, try a bowl of scouse, the hearty stew the city's people are named after.

During the day, St George's Hall is a stunning neoclassical building, and the Walker Art Gallery and World Museum are just next door and free to visit. Music fans can pay a visit to the Cavern Club on Mathew Street, famous for its links with the Beatles, or catch a ferry across the Mersey for some of the best views of the city skyline.
